verses.original: וְשַׁ֣בְתִּֽי אֲנִ֗י וָאֶרְאֶה֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הָ֣עֲשֻׁקִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשִׂ֖ים תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀ דִּמְעַ֣ת הָעֲשֻׁקִ֗ים וְאֵ֤ין לָהֶם֙ מְנַחֵ֔ם כֹּ֔חַ וּמִיַּ֤ד עֹֽשְׁקֵיהֶם֙ וְאֵ֥ין לָהֶ֖ם מְנַחֵֽם׃
verses.transliteration: wə·šaḇ·tî ’ă·nî wā·’er·’eh ’eṯ- kāl- hā·‘ă·šu·qîm ’ă·šer na·‘ă·śîm ta·ḥaṯ haš·šā·meš wə·hin·nêh dim·‘aṯ hā·‘ă·šu·qîm wə·’ên lā·hem mə·na·ḥêm kō·aḥ ū·mî·yaḏ ‘ō·šə·qê·hem wə·’ên lā·hem mə·na·ḥêm
verses.literal: Again [I looked] and I considered - all the oppression - taking place under the sun [I] saw the tears of the oppressed and they had no comforter the power [lay] in the hands of their oppressors and there was no comforter

verses.original: אֲנִ֛י אֶת־ וְשַׁבֵּ֧חַ הַמֵּתִ֖ים שֶׁכְּבָ֣ר מֵ֑תוּ מִן־ הַ֣חַיִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥מָּה עֲדֶֽנָה׃ חַיִּ֖ים
verses.transliteration: ’ă·nî ’eṯ- wə·šab·bê·aḥ ham·mê·ṯîm šek·kə·ḇār mê·ṯū min- ha·ḥay·yîm ’ă·šer hêm·māh ‘ă·ḏe·nāh ḥay·yîm
verses.literal: So I - admired the dead who had already died above the living who . . . are still alive

verses.original: וְטוֹב֙ מִשְּׁנֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ לֹ֣א עֲדֶ֖ן הָיָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ רָאָה֙ אֶת־ הָרָ֔ע הַמַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ṭō·wḇ miš·šə·nê·hem ’êṯ ’ă·šer- lō ‘ă·ḏen hā·yāh ’ă·šer lō- rā·’āh ’eṯ- hā·rā‘ ham·ma·‘ă·śeh ’ă·šer na·‘ă·śāh ta·ḥaṯ haš·šā·meš
verses.literal: But better than both - is he who has not yet existed who has not seen - the evil . . . that is done under the sun

verses.original: אֲנִ֜י אֶת־ וְרָאִ֨יתִֽי כָּל־ עָמָ֗ל וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ כִּשְׁר֣וֹן הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה כִּ֛י הִ֥יא אִ֖ישׁ קִנְאַת־ מֵרֵעֵ֑הוּ זֶ֥ה גַּם־ הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃
verses.transliteration: ’ă·nî ’eṯ- wə·rā·’î·ṯî kāl- ‘ā·māl wə·’êṯ kāl- kiš·rō·wn ham·ma·‘ă·śeh kî hî ’îš qin·’aṯ- mê·rê·‘ê·hū zeh gam- he·ḇel ū·rə·‘ūṯ rū·aḥ
verses.literal: I - saw that all labor and - success . . . spring from . . . a man’s envy of his neighbor This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind

verses.original: הַכְּסִיל֙ חֹבֵ֣ק אֶת־ יָדָ֔יו וְאֹכֵ֖ל אֶת־ בְּשָׂרֽוֹ׃
verses.literal: The fool folds - his hands and consumes - his own flesh

verses.original: ט֕וֹב מְלֹ֥א כַ֖ף נָ֑חַת מִמְּלֹ֥א חָפְנַ֛יִם עָמָ֖ל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃
verses.transliteration: ṭō·wḇ mə·lō ḵap̄ nā·ḥaṯ mim·mə·lō ḥā·p̄ə·na·yim ‘ā·māl ū·rə·‘ūṯ rū·aḥ
verses.literal: Better one handful . . . with tranquility than two handfuls . . . with toil and pursuit of the wind

verses.original: וְשַׁ֧בְתִּי אֲנִ֛י וָאֶרְאֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
verses.literal: Again I saw futility under the sun

verses.original: יֵ֣שׁ אֶחָד֩ וְאֵ֨ין שֵׁנִ֜י אֵֽין־ ל֗וֹ גַּ֣ם בֵּ֧ן וָאָ֣ח וְאֵ֥ין קֵץ֙ לְכָל־ עֲמָל֔וֹ עֵינָיו גַּם־ לֹא־ תִשְׂבַּ֣ע עֹ֑שֶׁר וּלְמִ֣י׀ אֲנִ֣י עָמֵ֗ל וּמְחַסֵּ֤ר אֶת־ נַפְשִׁי֙ מִטּוֹבָ֔ה זֶ֥ה גַּם־ הֶ֛בֶל רָ֖ע הֽוּא׃ וְעִנְיַ֥ן
verses.transliteration: yêš ’e·ḥāḏ wə·’ên šê·nî ’ên- lōw gam bên wā·’āḥ wə·’ên qêṣ lə·ḵāl ‘ă·mā·lōw ʿē·nå̄w gam- lō- ṯiś·ba‘ ‘ō·šer ū·lə·mî ’ă·nî ‘ā·mêl ū·mə·ḥas·sêr ’eṯ- nap̄·šî miṭ·ṭō·w·ḇāh zeh gam- he·ḇel rā‘ hū wə·‘in·yan
verses.literal: There is a man all alone . . . without even a son or brother And though there is no end - to his labor his eyes are still not content with his wealth For whom do I toil and bereave - my soul of enjoyment This too is futile a miserable . . . task

verses.original: הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם טוֹבִ֥ים מִן־ הָאֶחָ֑ד אֲשֶׁ֧ר יֵשׁ־ לָהֶ֛ם ט֖וֹב שָׂכָ֥ר בַּעֲמָלָֽם׃
verses.transliteration: haš·šə·na·yim ṭō·w·ḇîm min- hā·’e·ḥāḏ ’ă·šer yêš- lā·hem ṭō·wḇ śā·ḵār ba·‘ă·mā·lām
verses.literal: Two are better than one because they have . . . a good return for their labor

verses.original: כִּ֣י אִם־ הָאֶחָ֖ד יִפֹּ֔לוּ חֲבֵר֑וֹ יָקִ֣ים אֶת־ וְאִ֣יל֗וֹ הָֽאֶחָד֙ שֶׁיִּפּ֔וֹל וְאֵ֥ין שֵׁנִ֖י לַהֲקִימֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: kî ’im- hā·’e·ḥāḏ yip·pō·lū ḥă·ḇê·rōw yā·qîm ’eṯ- wə·’î·lōw hā·’e·ḥāḏ še·yip·pō·wl wə·’ên šê·nî la·hă·qî·mōw
verses.literal: For if one falls down his companion can lift him up - but pity the one who falls without another to help him up

verses.original: גַּ֛ם אִם־ שְׁנַ֖יִם יִשְׁכְּב֥וּ וְחַ֣ם לָהֶ֑ם אֵ֥יךְ וּלְאֶחָ֖ד יֵחָֽם׃
verses.transliteration: gam ’im- šə·na·yim yiš·kə·ḇū wə·ḥam lā·hem ’êḵ ū·lə·’e·ḥāḏ yê·ḥām
verses.literal: Again if two lie down together they will keep warm but how can one keep warm {alone}

verses.original: וְאִֽם־ הָאֶחָ֔ד יִתְקְפוֹ֙ הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם יַעַמְד֣וּ נֶגְדּ֑וֹ וְהַחוּט֙ הַֽמְשֻׁלָּ֔שׁ לֹ֥א בִמְהֵרָ֖ה יִנָּתֵֽק׃
verses.transliteration: wə·’im- hā·’e·ḥāḏ yiṯ·qə·p̄ōw haš·šə·na·yim ya·‘am·ḏū neḡ·dōw wə·ha·ḥūṭ ham·šul·lāš lō ḇim·hê·rāh yin·nā·ṯêq
verses.literal: And though one may be overpowered two can resist - Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken

verses.original: ט֛וֹב מִסְכֵּ֖ן וְחָכָ֑ם יֶ֥לֶד זָקֵן֙ וּכְסִ֔יל מִמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־ עֽוֹד׃ יָדַ֥ע לְהִזָּהֵ֖ר
verses.transliteration: ṭō·wḇ mis·kên wə·ḥā·ḵām ye·leḏ zā·qên ū·ḵə·sîl mim·me·leḵ ’ă·šer lō- ‘ō·wḏ yā·ḏa‘ lə·hiz·zā·hêr
verses.literal: Better is a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take a warning

verses.original: כִּֽי־ יָצָ֣א מִבֵּ֥ית הָסוּרִ֖ים לִמְלֹ֑ךְ כִּ֛י גַּ֥ם נוֹלַ֥ד רָֽשׁ׃ בְּמַלְכוּת֖וֹ
verses.transliteration: kî- yā·ṣā mib·bêṯ hā·sū·rîm lim·lōḵ kî gam nō·w·laḏ rāš bə·mal·ḵū·ṯōw
verses.literal: For [the youth] has come from the prison . . . to the kingship though . . . he was born poor in his own kingdom

verses.original: רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הַ֣חַיִּ֔ים הַֽמְהַלְּכִ֖ים תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ עִ֚ם הַשֵּׁנִ֔י הַיֶּ֣לֶד אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: rā·’î·ṯî ’eṯ- kāl- ha·ḥay·yîm ham·hal·lə·ḵîm ta·ḥaṯ haš·šā·meš ‘im haš·šê·nî hay·ye·leḏ ’ă·šer ya·‘ă·mōḏ taḥ·tāw
verses.literal: I saw that - all who lived and walked under the sun followed this second one the youth who succeeded [the king]

verses.original: אֵֽין־ קֵ֣ץ לְכָל־ הָעָ֗ם לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־ הָיָה֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם גַּ֥ם ב֑וֹ לֹ֣א יִשְׂמְחוּ־ הָאַחֲרוֹנִ֖ים זֶ֥ה כִּֽי־ גַם־ הֶ֖בֶל וְרַעְי֥וֹן רֽוּחַ׃
verses.transliteration: ’ên- qêṣ lə·ḵāl hā·‘ām lə·ḵōl ’ă·šer- hā·yāh lip̄·nê·hem gam ḇōw lō yiś·mə·ḥū- hā·’a·ḥă·rō·w·nîm zeh kî- ḡam- he·ḇel wə·ra‘·yō·wn rū·aḥ
verses.literal: There is no limit to all the people . . . who were before them Yet [the successor] will not be celebrated by those who come even later This too . . . is futile and a pursuit of the wind
